text:
Alex Lyon put it bluntly in his season debut, and the reporters covering Buffalo agree: the Sabres can't pretend about where they are. They're winless in four (0-3-1), outscored 17-6, and sit at 8-8-4 with 20 points. Our playoff odds are down to 23%.

The strange part is that the season-long process is fine. Buffalo has taken 50% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) and its shot-attempt share is healthy. The problem is finishing: the Sabres have scored about 9.4 fewer goals than their chances usually produce, the worst kind of gap for a team already behind. Jake Oettinger shutting them out twice this season didn't help.

The goaltending story is the other headline. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen was pulled in the rout by Tampa Bay, Colten Ellis struggled in relief, and Lyon's return gives them a steadier option. Collectively the goalies have allowed 3.6 more goals than expected.

There is something to build on. Jack Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson have taken 59% of the expected goals together and 65% of the shot attempts, the best line on the team. Tage Thompson keeps scoring. What we'd watch: whether the finishing turns before the standings make the decision for them.
